subject: computer-science
title: Data Representation: Foundations
welcome_lead: Computers see only 1s and 0s — let's learn how they encode everything.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science adventure on binary, denary and hexadecimal foundations.
final_note: You can now translate between the three number bases computers use.

concepts.def: Base-16, a shorthand for binary (0–9, A–F).
A bit is one binary digit; 8 bits make a byte.
ASCII and Unicode represent text as binary codes.
Images stored as pixels with a colour depth.
Sound sampled at a rate and bit depth to store digitally.

walkthroughs.body_html:
• Binary (base 2): only 0 and 1
  • Denary (base 10): 0-9
  • Hex (base 16): 0-9, A=10, B=11, C=12, D=13, E=14, F=15

Each hex digit = 4 binary bits. 1111 = F. 1111 1111 = FF = 255.

Hex is shorter and human-friendly: A4 is easier to write than 10100100.

mcqs.q: The largest denary value that can be stored in one byte is:
Does the binary number 10 mean ten?
options: Yes - 10 is ten no matter what base it is written in.
No - in binary, 10 means one two and zero units, which is the denary value two; the same symbols mean different values in different bases.
65 - A is always its ASCII code.
No - binary 10 means one hundred.

mcqs.q: Is the largest value in a byte 256?
options: Yes - a byte's maximum is 1024.
Yes - eight bits count up to exactly 256.
No - binary 10 means one hundred.
No - a byte has 256 different patterns, but they run from 0 to 255, so the largest value is 255.

mcqs.q: What does the hexadecimal digit A represent in denary?
options: 1 - A is the first letter so it stands for one.
65 - A is always its ASCII code.
No - binary 10 means one hundred.
10 - the letters A to F continue counting after 9, representing denary 10 to 15.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Byte”?
options: A group of 8 bits, able to represent 256 different values; file sizes are measured in bytes and their multiples.
Half a byte - a group of 4 bits - which is exactly the amount of binary represented by one hexadecimal digit.
A binary digit, 0 or 1 - the smallest unit of data a computer stores, corresponding to one two-state switch in hardware.
The base-16 system using 0-9 and A-F; each hex digit stands for exactly four bits, giving a compact way to write binary.
